errors.quote: Over $\mathbb F_2,$ norm-one tensors of indicators or coordinate units give each nonzero residual an orthonormal basis
errors.problem: The norm-one tensors only show that each residual contains a vector of norm one, i.e. is nonalternating; with nondegeneracy (not mentioned), the orthonormal basis then comes from the splitting theorem for nondegenerate nonalternating binary symmetric spaces (paper, proof of Lemma motif-residuals). As worded, the tensors seem to supply the basis themselves.

The same symbol $t_T$ is used in rows 2 and 5 of the gate table for different triples (the X-side gate's triple at time 2, the Y-side gate's triple at time 5); read with one $T$, the $2\to5$ inclusion $P\otimes\langle t_T\rangle\subset P\otimes t_T^\perp$ would be false since $\langle t_T,t_T\rangle\neq0$. The paper writes $t_X,t_Y$ and says that for a gate indexed by a physical bank triple, $t$ is that triple's indicator.
